To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variance– mean relationship of parasite numbers per square meter is well described by Taylor's Law and that the spatial distribution is strongly influenced by high local correlations of parasite loads of host individuals.
the variance– mean relationship of parasite numbers per square meter of littoral zone is described very well by Taylor's law but not by the negative binomial variance–mean relationship.
the spatial distribution in space of parasites depends on the distribution of the parasites in hosts and on the spatial distribution of the hosts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial distribution of individuals within species and its implications for parasite control and conservation.
the spatial distribution of individuals in populations, and we develop a theory of the spatial distribution of a parasite species based on the distribution in its host population.
spatial patterns in the abundance of parasites and hosts in a habitat and how they are related.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial distributions of parasites depend crucially on high correlations of hosts' loads.

the variance– mean relationship of parasites per square-meter habitat is very well described empirically by TL, and this relationship can be used to predict the variance–mean and spatial distributions of parasites in a square meter with a high degree of accuracy.
the spatial distribution in a lake is determined by a combination of Taylor's law and perfect interhost correlation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial distribution and abundance of parasites in the littorals of the four studied lakes can be predicted by the abundance of the hosts and the distribution of parasites within the hosts.

the spatial distribution and abundance of a parasite is determined by the spatial distribution and density of its host, and the variance of parasite abundance within hosts is described well by Taylor's law, which is a power-law relationship between the mean and the variance.

the spatial distribution and abundance of parasites is a function of both the abundance of parasites in hosts (which can be predicted by Taylor's law) and the spatial distribution and aggregation of hosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial distributional properties of parasites are strongly determined by the spatial distributional structure of the hosts.
the distribution of parasites within hosts is a major determinant of the spatial distribution of parasite individuals.

the spatial distribution and abundance of parasites depend on the spatial distribution and correlation structure of hosts, as well as the spatial distribution of resources and the spatial distribution and dynamics of parasites.
